text: Clear and dry the whole way. Views were worth every step.
The falls are absolutely roaring with runoff. Sloppy for the first mile, then it dries out nicely. Sunscreen is non-negotiable up there.
Creek crossings are all rock-hoppable at the moment.
Took the kids up. Frost on the boardwalks first thing in the morning, slick as glass.
No obstacles, no issues, just a great day out. Would do it again tomorrow.
Quick morning lap. Paintbrush and lupine everywhere right now. Would do it again tomorrow.
Fireweed lining the old burn section, gorgeous. Clear and dry the whole way.
First time on this one. Clear and dry the whole way.
Clear and dry the whole way.
Trail runner here. Barely any bugs today, a nice surprise for this time of year. The rocky stretch near the overlook is dry and grippy.
Trail runner here. Popular with families on the first mile, thins out fast after that.
Back again after a few weeks. Seasonal streams mostly dry, carry more water than you think. Highly recommend a weekday if you can swing it.
A couple of downed branches across the trail, all easy step-overs. Everything melted out and dried up, prime conditions. Great day overall.
Out and back before lunch. No obstacles, no issues, just a great day out.
Seasonal streams mostly dry, carry more water than you think.
Some erosion on the outer edge of the switchbacks, stay inside.
The avalanche chutes are green and full of glacier lilies. Highly recommend a weekday if you can swing it.
Out and back before lunch. Creek crossings are all rock-hoppable at the moment. Parking lot was full by 8am, arrive early.
Saw a sow with two cubs grazing near the berry patches at the meadow edge. She was calm but we gave them a very wide berth.
Ranger at the junction told us a food-conditioned bear has been hanging around, getting into packs left on the ground. Keep everything on you.
Bear warnings posted at the trailhead this morning. Fresh scat and diggings right on the tread past the second switchback. Made plenty of noise the whole way.
Trail was closed for a few hours today due to bear activity near the meadow. Reopened by early afternoon. Carry spray and hike in groups.
A couple of downed branches across the trail, all easy step-overs. Black flies swarming in the still sections, keep moving.
Clear and dry the whole way.
Solo trip midweek. Spray from the cascade keeps the lower trail damp all day. Waterbars are doing their job, tread is in great shape.
